tools.name: report_result
tools.description:
Hand in this task's report once its work is committed.
Give the outcome, a summary of at most 200 characters, the files changed, the tests you ran, the decisions you settled, open questions for him and follow-ups. Jocasta stores it with the thread and its review reads it; a test you mark passed is your claim, the review runs its own.

summary.description: What the task did, at most 200 characters

command.description: The test command as you ran it

tests.description: The tests you ran and whether each passed

decisions.description: Choices you settled that later work shouldn't reopen

tools.name: check
tools.description:
Run this task's checks on the worktree as it is now, instead of tests in bash.
The checks are the project's mise verify/test task and the task's done_when commands. Results are cached by git tree, so an unchanged tree answers at once. Replies `checks: PASS (tree …)`, or FAIL with one line per gate, the failing tests, the log's path and the narrowest command to rerun.

tools.name: projects
tools.description:
His projects, their threads and states, and leftover worktrees.
Each thread's state, open threads touching the same files, and leftover worktrees (closed in herdr, still on disk) with their branch, commits ahead and changes.

tools.name: thread_start
tools.description:
Start a thread in a project, in plan mode on its own worktree and branch.
It opens as a worktree workspace under its project's, running omp in plan mode. The brief is its first message; it and done_when go into its task file and its system prompt, and its review runs each done_when command. With heavy, it runs on his slow role (his strongest model) from plan to execution. In a project other than the one of the last pane he focused: Jocasta asks him first (Allow / Deny); Deny, or no answer within 2 minutes, refuses it and the reply says so.

title.description: Short title; its slug names the branch

done_when.description: Commands that must pass for the task to be done, e.g. bun test test/auth.test.ts

heavy.description: Run the thread on his slow role, his strongest model, for ambitious or open-ended work (a migration, a deep bug, a large refactor); it spends his Fable allowance fastest. Leave it out otherwise

tools.name: thread_status
tools.description:
Threads' states and each one's last answer; one thread when named.
Each with the open threads of the same project that touch the same files.

tools.name: thread_send
tools.description:
Send a message to a thread: steering when busy, a new run when idle.
A thread awaiting his answer to a question, or his approval of its plan, refuses it: he answers in its pane.

tools.name: thread_stop
tools.description:
Stop a thread's current run.
One Escape into its pane: the run ends, the thread keeps its worktree and work, and thread_send starts it again.

tools.name: thread_finish
tools.description:
Finish a thread by merge or PR, only on his explicit word.
Only a reviewed thread, when he explicitly says to: merge squash-merges its branch into trunk in the main checkout (when trunk moved since its review, trunk is merged into the branch and it is tested and reviewed again first; it merges only when that passes); pr has the thread push its branch and open a PR with gh. Then its worktree and workspace are removed (and the branch after a merge). Jocasta asks him first (Allow / Deny); Deny, or no answer within 2 minutes, refuses it and the reply says so. The reply says when its last review wasn't a pass and which open threads touch the same files. A refusal leaves everything in place and says why.

tools.name: show
tools.description:
Open a whiteboard review in his browser.
Create it first with whiteboard's session_create and pass its sessionId; an unknown id is refused with the reason.

review.description: The review's sessionId from whiteboard's session_create

tools.name: today
tools.description:
His day: meetings, what needs him, threads running and finished.
Today's meetings, what needs him (reviews requested, red pipelines, blocked threads, reminders), threads running and finished since yesterday. Use it when he asks what's today.

tools.name: note
tools.description:
File his "note: …" into a project's next work.
A note always belongs to a project; ask him which one only when you can't tell.

tools.name: remind
tools.description:
File his "remind me …" into today at a time; it is raised when due.
Ask him when only if he gave no time you can tell.

text.description: What to remind him of, in his words

at.description: HH:MM (the next time it comes) or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, his local time

project.description: Project name or id, when it belongs to one

tools.name: inbox_done
tools.description:
Mark an inbox note or reminder done when he says it is.
The id is its number: note's and remind's replies give it, and today lists notes as (#N); an id that isn't open is refused.

tools.name: worklog
tools.description:
Write his worklog: one entry per project, with time per project.
The entries come from the day's threads and his commits. Entries he edited are kept as he left them.

project.description: Project name or id; every project when left out

tools.name: lesson
tools.description:
Save a lesson for a project, only after he said yes.
His yes is "make that a lesson", or yes to your offer. A lesson is something non-obvious, durable and material that its threads read before planning and its reviews check. A lesson of the same title is replaced. Jocasta shows him its text first (Allow / Deny); Deny, or no answer within 2 minutes, saves nothing and the reply says so.

title.description: Short title; it names the lesson's file

applies_when.description: When it applies, e.g. adding a git call to the service

rule.description: The rule in 1–3 lines, then why: what went wrong

source.description: Where it came from, e.g. <project>/<thread title>, commit <sha>

retire_when.description: An outside condition that makes it obsolete, if any

tools.name: big_picture_review
tools.description:
Start a project's big-picture review; its result comes as an [event].
One read-only review of everything merged into its trunk in the past 7 days against its rules and lessons, looking for design drift across changes. It starts at once and its result arrives minutes later as one [event] line.

tools.name: worktree_remove
tools.description:
Remove a leftover worktree, only when he says to.
A leftover is a thread folder closed in herdr, still on disk; `projects` lists them. One with uncommitted changes is refused; its branch stays. Jocasta asks him first (Allow / Deny); Deny, or no answer within 2 minutes, refuses it and the reply says so.

path.description: The leftover's folder, as `projects` lists it
